description: Relay protocol v1 (spec/relay.md): derivations, messages, and scripted runs of one self-hosted relay. Replay model in relay.md section 14.

malformed.why: REGISTER with a token and no threshold

scenarios.name: register_and_call
scenarios.notes: A listed caller reaches a registered target: INCOMING on the registration connection, an accept leg on a new connection, SPLICED on both legs, peer messages forwarded both ways. A bulk call is its own circuit; one leg closing closes only its circuit.

scenarios.name: unlisted_equals_offline
scenarios.notes: An unlisted caller, an offline target, an unknown handle, a bad proof and a target with no allow-set yet all get UNREACHABLE exactly at the refusal deadline (500 ms after the CALL), and nothing before. A listed caller to an online target that never accepts gets UNREACHABLE at the accept wait, never before the refusal deadline.

scenarios.name: register_other_key
scenarios.notes: A handle is derived from the key that proved itself: someone else's key with the attacker's proof, an unauthorized key, and a proof over a handle that does not match the key are all REFUSED(not_authorized). The real key registers.

scenarios.name: register_replayed
scenarios.notes: A REGISTER replayed on another connection, and one proved for another relay, are REFUSED(not_authorized); the original registration is untouched.

scenarios.name: call_replayed_other_connection
scenarios.notes: A listed caller's CALL replayed verbatim on another connection is refused like any other: UNREACHABLE at the refusal deadline.

scenarios.name: call_other_relay
scenarios.notes: A call proof made for another relay, and one made for the other class, are refused at the refusal deadline.

scenarios.name: removed_caller_closed
scenarios.notes: An allow-set without the caller closes its spliced circuit (both legs, caller first) and its waiting call with 4000 at once, before ALLOW_SET_OK. Its next call is refused.

scenarios.name: removal_leaves_others
scenarios.notes: Removing one caller closes only that caller's circuit; another caller's circuit keeps forwarding.

scenarios.name: join_without_tag
scenarios.notes: A JOIN with a wrong tag, with the tag hash in place of the tag, or with the tag of an expired invitation is refused at the refusal deadline. The right tag is admitted: INCOMING with kind join and no caller.

scenarios.name: preaccept_over_budget
scenarios.notes: An unpromoted join circuit carries at most RELAY_PREACCEPT_BYTES (65 536) of peer bytes each way; the message that would go over closes both legs with 4006. A join circuit also closes, 4006, when its invitation expires on the relay's wall clock.

scenarios.name: preaccept_per_target
scenarios.notes: At most RELAY_PREACCEPT_PER_TARGET (4) join circuits per handle: the fifth JOIN is refused at the refusal deadline; once one ends, a JOIN is admitted again.

scenarios.name: accept_wrong_key
scenarios.notes: An ACCEPT signed by another key, naming an unknown circuit, or naming another handle is REFUSED(not_authorized) and the circuit keeps waiting; the target's own ACCEPT then splices it.

scenarios.name: accept_wait_expires
scenarios.notes: An admitted call with no accept leg gets UNREACHABLE when the accept wait fires; a late ACCEPT is refused like an unknown circuit.

scenarios.name: successor_without_current_key
scenarios.notes: A SUCCESSOR whose current-key proof is not by the registered key is REFUSED(not_authorized) and closes the registration connection; its spliced circuit keeps running and the new key stays unauthorized.

scenarios.name: successor_unauthorized_current
scenarios.notes: A SUCCESSOR proved by both keys authorizes the new key and supersedes the current one (no answer). The superseded key, still registered, cannot vouch for another successor. The new key registers on its own connection.

scenarios.name: successor_drop
scenarios.notes: After a SUCCESSOR both keys register during the overlap. At the drop time the superseded key leaves the list and its registration and circuits close with 4000; it can no longer register.

scenarios.name: allow_set_lower_sequence
scenarios.notes: After the first allow-set of a registration, a sequence not above the last one is ignored (no answer, no change). A new registration accepts any first sequence.

scenarios.name: promote_unlisted
scenarios.notes: A PROMOTE naming a fingerprint not in the current allow-set, or a join circuit that is not spliced, is ignored: the circuit stays under the pre-accept budget.

scenarios.name: join_promoted
scenarios.notes: After pairing over a join circuit the target lists the new caller and sends PROMOTE: the circuit leaves the pre-accept budget and the join count, and is that caller's call circuit from then on, closed with 4000 when the caller is removed.

scenarios.name: circuits_outlive_registration
scenarios.notes: A circuit belongs to the handle: when the registration connection closes, a spliced circuit keeps forwarding and a waiting one can still be accepted. A new registration starts with no allow-set, so calls are refused until it pushes one; a second registration of the handle replaces the first (4005).

scenarios.name: enrollment
scenarios.notes: ENROLL with a valid code removes the code and authorizes the key, durably, before REGISTERED. A bad proof is REFUSED(not_authorized) and keeps the code; a used, expired or unknown code is REFUSED(enrollment). The enrolled key then registers normally.

scenarios.name: revoke
scenarios.notes: The operator revokes a key: its registration and every circuit of its handle close with 4000 (caller legs first), and it can no longer register.

scenarios.name: keepalive_and_idle
scenarios.notes: A connection with no first message closes 4002 after RELAY_HELLO_WAIT_MS. The relay PINGs a registration RELAY_KEEPALIVE_MS after it last sent, answers a PING with a PONG, and closes it 4002 RELAY_REGISTRATION_IDLE_MS after it last received. A spliced circuit with no bytes for RELAY_CIRCUIT_IDLE_MS closes 4002.

scenarios.name: protocol_errors
scenarios.notes: A malformed message, a relay-to-client type, a hosted REGISTER in self mode, a message the role does not allow, anything on a leg before SPLICED, and a second REGISTER all close the connection with 1002 at once and nothing else is sent. A leg that ends this way ends its circuit; a refused caller that errs gets no UNREACHABLE.

scenarios.name: connection_limits
scenarios.notes: With RELAY_CONNECTIONS_PER_IP 2, a third connection from one address is closed 4006 before RELAY_HELLO (no nonce drawn); an accept leg stops counting against its address once its ACCEPT arrives. RELAY_CIRCUITS_PER_CALLER 2 refuses a third call at the refusal deadline. RELAY_ACCEPT_LEGS_PER_HANDLE 1 refuses a second accept leg with REFUSED(limit).
